score.note: Third pass, evidence-grounded against games/gs1/asm/080d59b0.s directly (not a permutation search). Confirmed from the retained assembly that the reference prologue does use `ldmia r3!, {r1}` (bytes 0x0e-0x1e: `ldr r6,[pc,#92]; adds r3,r6,#0; ldmia r3!,{r1}; ldr r3,[r3,#0]; ...; mov r9,r1; add r3,r9`), so applied the raw `void **` cursor idiom already proved in the adopted member_orbit/run.c and in 080e01e4.c: `heap_cache = (void **)0x03001EEC; cursor = heap_cache; work = *cursor++; draw_destination = *cursor;`. This alone regressed the score (286->307) because it left `heap_cache` unused after the initial reads while the reference keeps r6 (holding 0x03001EEC) alive and reuses it: `ldr r2,[r6,#28]` and `ldr r6,[r6,#32]` read the two DrawRectangleFn pointers at 0x03001F08/0x03001F0C as `heap_cache[7]`/`heap_cache[8]` rather than through fresh pc-relative literal-pool loads of those fixed addresses. Rewriting the two `*(DrawRectangleFn*)0x03001Fxx` reads as `heap_cache[7]`/`heap_cache[8]`, hoisted into two named locals `callback_a`/`callback_b` at the exact reference positions -- `callback_a` read between the two `Func_080ed408` calls (matching `ldr r2,[r6,#28]` immediately after the first call), `callback_b` read after the second call and before the 32-entry sprite-pool loop (matching the `.L0:`-label `ldr r6,[r6,#32]`) -- dropped differing_halfwords from 307 to 277, better than both the pre-cursor baseline (286) and the naive cursor-only attempt (307). This differs from this dossier's own previously-rejected callback-hoist experiment in two ways confirmed against the .s file: the reference genuinely does hoist-and-stack-spill both callback reads early (`str r2,[sp,#12]` / `str r6,[sp,#16]`), so hoisting itself is correct; what the earlier attempt got wrong was reading them via fresh fixed-address casts (forcing new pc-relative literal loads) instead of heap_cache-relative indexing off the still-live r6, and hoisting both together after the second Func_080ed408 call instead of interleaved individually between/after the two calls as the reference actually schedules them.

rejected_experiments: Struct-typed single read of the two leading 0x03001EEC/0x03001EF0 globals (hoping to reproduce the reference's ldmia r3!,{r1} load-multiple prologue): compiled to two ordinary back-to-back ldr instructions instead of ldmia and regressed differing_halfwords from 281 to 317; reverted to two independent raw-pointer dereferences.

Hoisting the two function-pointer reads at 0x03001F08/0x03001F0C (draw_rectangle/alt_draw_rectangle) into named locals read once right after the two Func_080ed408 calls, matching the reference's own early read+stack-spill of these values: this is structurally what the reference does (str to sp+12/sp+16, later reload), but declaring them as ordinary C locals kept them live across the entire 148-frame outer loop in this compiler's allocator and regressed the score (281->309); reverted to inline point-of-use dereferences of the fixed addresses, which the compiler happened to schedule closer to the reference's own load sites.

Applying the void** cursor idiom (`cursor = heap_cache; work = *cursor++; draw_destination = *cursor;`) alone, still reading the two DrawRectangleFn pointers via fresh `*(DrawRectangleFn*)0x03001Fxx` casts: regressed 286->307 because it discarded `heap_cache` after the initial reads instead of reusing it (as the reference's r6 does) for the two later offset reads. Superseded by heap_cache[7]/heap_cache[8] indexing (see score.note); the cursor idiom itself was correct evidence, only the surrounding source shape needed to keep heap_cache alive too.

Semantic summary: a battle-presentation sub-effect. Seeds a 32-entry sprite-record pool at 0x02010000 with randomized initial falling parameters, opens two display windows (ids 46 and 47), then runs 148 frames. Each frame conditionally walks the active work-target's member list (drawing/positioning each member's portrait via Func_08004cb4 and occasionally cueing Func_080d6888), then integrates simple bounce physics (gravity accumulator, velocity, halved rebound damping) over the first 12 sprite records and draws each active one through one of two rectangle-callback function pointers selected by a phase-derived 0-7 'kind' value, alternating draw target by whether kind is 0-3 or 4-7.

The 'wrong' class and the 277/278 residual are now dominated by two specific, already cross-family-documented open compiler questions rather than an unrecovered source shape: (1) the reference keeps `work` in r9 for the whole function, but this compiler keeps choosing fp for it in this owner; tracing the .s file shows this is not cosmetic -- `facing` (`*(s32*)0x03001E80`, re-read once per outer-loop iteration) lives in fp for the reference's entire 148-frame loop body (never spilled), which is only possible because r9, not fp, holds `work` there. In this candidate, since `work` occupies fp, `facing` has no free callee-saved register left and gets spilled to sp+20 every iteration instead, which is most of the remaining 12-byte (3-word) frame-size gap (52 vs the reference's 40) and its knock-on pool/offset churn. 080dc1ec.json's rejected experiments already showed this compiler's fp/r9 choice is insensitive to declaration order and block scope for this same shared work-block idiom, so this was not re-attempted here as a blind lever. (2) `Func_080072f4`'s 5th argument (`callback`, a `DrawRectangleFn`) is passed through r4 in the reference rather than the stack slot ordinary APCS would use for a 5th word argument; 080dc1ec.json's rejected experiments already confirmed no adopted sibling source anywhere in games/gs1/src/ calls Func_080072f4 directly with 7 literal arguments and reproduces this, making it a genuinely unprecedented, unresolved calling-convention question, not something to guess at here. Because this candidate instead passes callback+w+h all through the stack, the compiler's own cross-jump optimizer merges the tail of the two Func_080072f4 call sites (kind<=3 vs kind>3) into shared code, which the reference's r4-argument version apparently does not do (its two call sites stay fully separate in the .s file) -- another visible symptom of the same open question rather than a new, independently fixable defect.
No GS2 or external source was used; no other Golden Sun decompilation project was consulted.
